examples.en: I heat the milk slowly over low heat.
Heat the meat thoroughly before eating.
I heated the pot for too long.
Heated food tastes different once it cools.
You only need to heat it for 30 seconds in the microwave.

examples.ko: 쇠를 가열하는 모습을 과학 시간에 봤어요.
examples.en: We saw iron being heated in science class.

explain: 요리나 실험 설명서에서 '충분히 가열하세요'처럼 많이 보여요. 집에서는 식은 음식을 '데우다', 물을 '끓이다'라고 더 자주 말해요. '가열하다'는 열을 주는 행동 자체에 초점이 있어서 방법을 설명할 때 좋아요.
explain_en: It appears often in recipes and experiment instructions, as in 충분히 가열하세요. At home people usually say 데우다 for reheating food and 끓이다 for boiling water. 가열하다 focuses on the act of applying heat, which suits explaining a method.

examples.en: My father farms a small field himself.

examples.ko: 남의 땅을 빌려 경작하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people rent other people's land and farm it.
In this area, they mainly grow barley.
The ground is dry, so it is hard to cultivate.
In the old days, they cultivated rice fields with cows.

examples.ko: 이 산은 경작하지 않는 땅이라 나무가 많아요.
examples.en: This mountain is uncultivated land, so there are many trees.

explain: 일상에서는 '농사를 짓다'가 더 자연스럽고, 경작하다는 밭이나 논 같은 땅을 목적어로 써서 조금 딱딱하게 들려요. '밭을 경작하다'처럼 땅이 대상이고, 곡식은 '보리를 경작하다'처럼 말할 수도 있어요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In daily talk '농사를 짓다' is more natural, and 경작하다 sounds a bit stiff, taking land like a field or paddy as its object. You can say '밭을 경작하다' (cultivate a field), and also '보리를 경작하다' for crops. It appears often in news and writing.

examples.ko: 인간과 자연의 공생을 위해 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: We must make an effort for the coexistence of humans and nature.

examples.ko: 꽃과 벌은 서로 도우며 공생 관계를 이루어요.
examples.en: Flowers and bees help each other and form a symbiotic relationship.

examples.ko: 도시에서 사람과 동물의 공생은 쉽지 않은 문제예요.
examples.en: Humans and animals living together in a city is not an easy issue.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 전통 시장과 대형 마트의 공생 방안을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: This town is looking for ways for the traditional market and big supermarkets to coexist.
I want to build a society where living together is possible.

examples.ko: 생물 시간에 공생과 기생의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In biology class, I learned the difference between symbiosis and parasitism.

explain: 생물 이야기에서는 '공생 관계'로 서로 도우며 사는 모습을 말하고, 사회 이야기에서는 사람과 자연, 서로 다른 집단이 함께 사는 것을 말해요. 비슷한 '공존'은 단순히 같이 있는 것에 더 가까워요. 반대로 한쪽만 이익을 보는 관계는 '기생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In biology it describes a relationship where living things help each other ('공생 관계'), and in social topics it describes humans and nature, or different groups, living together. The similar '공존' is closer to simply existing side by side. A relationship where only one side benefits is called '기생' (parasitism).

examples.ko: 새 기능의 구현은 다음 달에 끝나요.
examples.en: The implementation of the new feature will finish next month.
It takes time to carry an idea through to implementation.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 간단한 구현으로도 잘 작동해요.
examples.en: This app works well even with a simple implementation.
My goal is the realization of my dream.

examples.ko: 구현이 어려운 부분은 나중에 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to do the hard-to-implement part later.
One person handled both the design and implementation.

explain: 개발자들이 '기능 구현'이라고 많이 써요. 계획을 실제로 만들어 내는 것이고, 말로는 '만들다', '실현하다'도 써요. '구현'은 명사라 '구현하다', '구현되다'로 바꿔 써요.
explain_en: Developers say '기능 구현' constantly. It means turning a plan into something real; in speech '만들다' or '실현하다' also work. It's a noun, with '구현하다' and '구현되다' as verb forms.

examples.en: This app maximizes user convenience.
They raised the price to maximize profit.

examples.ko: 공부 효과를 극대화하려면 충분히 자야 해요.
examples.en: To maximize your study results, you need enough sleep.

examples.ko: 감독은 선수들의 장점을 극대화하는 작전을 짰어요.
examples.en: The coach made a plan that maximizes the players' strengths.

examples.ko: 햇빛을 많이 받도록 창을 크게 내서 채광을 극대화했어요.
examples.en: They made big windows to maximize natural light.

examples.ko: 재미를 극대화하기 위해 마지막에 반전을 넣었어요.
examples.en: They added a twist at the end to maximize the fun.

explain: '최대로 하다'를 한 단어로 말하는 거예요. 효과, 이익, 재미, 효율 같은 말과 자주 쓰여요. 반대말은 '극소화하다'나 '최소화하다'이고, 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a one-word way to say 'make as large as possible'. It often goes with effect, profit, fun and efficiency. The opposites are '극소화하다' and '최소화하다', and it appears a lot in news and explanatory writing.

examples.en: He scratched his head as if embarrassed.
When asked a question, he laughed while scratching the back of his head.

examples.ko: 아이가 코를 긁적이면서 대답을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The child scratched their nose and couldn't answer.

examples.ko: 어색할 때 저도 모르게 뺨을 긁적여요.
examples.en: When I feel awkward, I scratch my cheek without realizing it.

examples.ko: 동생이 머리를 긁적이는 걸 보니 뭔가 잘못했나 봐요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is scratching their head, so they must have done something wrong.
My friend was scratching the back of their neck out of embarrassment.

explain: 가려워서보다는 쑥스럽거나 난처할 때 손으로 슬쩍 긁는 동작에 자주 써요. 그냥 몸을 긁는 것은 '긁다'라고 해요. '머리를 긁적이다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is often used for lightly scratching with a hand when you feel shy or awkward, not because of real itching. Ordinary scratching is just '긁다'. '머리를 긁적이다' is the most common pairing.

examples.ko: 할머니가 졸린 눈을 껌벅대며 앉아 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother is sitting there blinking her sleepy eyes.
The cat is slowly blinking its eyes.
The puppy looked at me, blinking.

examples.ko: 눈을 자꾸 껌벅대는 걸 보니 졸린가 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you blink so much, you must be sleepy.
The signal was flashing, so I crossed in a hurry.
Instead of answering, he just blinked.

explain: '껌벅거리다'와 거의 같은 말로, 눈이나 불빛이 느릿하게 계속 깜빡일 때 써요. 졸리거나 어리둥절해서 눈만 껌벅대는 모습을 말할 때 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '껌벅거리다' and is used for eyes or lights blinking slowly and repeatedly. It suits someone blinking blankly when sleepy or puzzled.

examples.ko: 아기 강아지들이 담요 위에서 꼬물꼬물 움직여요.
examples.en: The puppies are squirming around on the blanket.
A caterpillar is crawling along the leaf, wriggling.

examples.ko: 아기 고양이들이 꼬물꼬물 엄마 곁으로 모여요.
examples.en: The kittens gather around their mother, wriggling along.
I saw tadpoles wriggling along as they swam.

examples.ko: 꼬물꼬물 기어 오는 아기가 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: The baby crawling toward me with little wriggles is so cute.
The ants are going along in a line, squirming.

explain: '꼬물거리다'의 부사로, 작고 귀여운 것이 천천히 자꾸 움직이는 모습에 써요. 손가락·발가락 같은 몸의 일부를 조금씩 움직일 때는 '꼼지락꼼지락'이 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the adverb of '꼬물거리다', used for small, cute things moving slowly and repeatedly. When you move a part of the body, like fingers or toes, bit by bit, '꼼지락꼼지락' fits better.

en: to dart one's tongue in and out

examples.en: The cat flicks its tongue while drinking milk.
The frog flicked its tongue to catch a fly.
I sat in front of the stove where the flames flickered.

examples.ko: 혀를 날름대지 마세요, 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Please don't flick your tongue; it doesn't look nice.
The baby flicks its tongue while waiting for its baby food.
When a snake flicks its tongue, I get scared for no reason.

explain: '날름거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, '-거리다'와 '-대다'는 서로 바꿔 써도 돼요. 혀나 불길이 빠르게 움직일 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '날름거리다', and '-거리다' and '-대다' are interchangeable here. Use it when a tongue or flame moves quickly.

examples.en: The child saw Mom and dashed over.

examples.ko: 소나기가 오자 사람들이 처마 밑으로 달음박질쳤어요.
examples.en: When the shower started, people dashed under the eaves.
I'm dashing to the station so I don't miss the last train.
The puppy is darting toward the ball.
I fell while dashing and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 숨이 차도록 달음박질쳐서 겨우 시간에 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I ran until I was out of breath and barely made it on time.

explain: 힘껏 빠르게 뛰어가는 모습을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '뛰어가다'가 더 흔하고, 활용은 '달음박질쳐요/달음박질쳤어요'처럼 해요.
explain_en: It describes running somewhere quickly with all your strength. In daily talk '뛰어가다' is more common, and it conjugates as '달음박질쳐요/달음박질쳤어요'.

examples.ko: 아기가 기저귀를 갈 때 다리를 바동거려요.
examples.en: The baby kicks and wriggles his legs when I change his diaper.

examples.ko: 잡힌 벌레가 손 안에서 바동거리고 있어요.
examples.en: The bug I caught is wriggling in my hand.

examples.ko: 물에 빠진 아이가 바동거리는 걸 보고 바로 뛰어들었어요.
examples.en: I saw the child flailing in the water and jumped in right away.
The child said he wouldn't go and kicked and squirmed on the floor.
The fish caught on the fishing line struggled until it was exhausted.
No matter how much you struggle like that, it's no use.

explain: 작은 몸이나 손발을 급하게 흔들며 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습이에요. '버둥거리다'와 같은 계열로, '바동'이 더 작고 가벼운 느낌을 줘요. 어려운 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓴다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a small body or limbs moving quickly as someone tries to get free. It belongs to the same family as '버둥거리다', with '바동' feeling smaller and lighter. It can also be used figuratively for striving hard to escape a bad situation.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 색 배합이 예뻐서 사진 찍는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: This shop has a lovely color combination, so many people take photos.

examples.ko: 요리사는 소스의 배합을 아무에게도 알려 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: The chef didn't tell anyone the blend of his sauce.

examples.ko: 사료 배합은 동물에 따라 달라져야 해요.
examples.en: The feed mix has to differ depending on the animal.

examples.ko: 옷은 색 배합에 따라 느낌이 많이 달라져요.
examples.en: The feel of an outfit changes a lot depending on the color combination.

examples.ko: 시멘트와 모래의 배합 비율을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: You have to keep the mixing ratio of cement and sand properly.

examples.ko: 세 가지 재료의 배합으로 새로운 맛이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new flavor came out of blending three ingredients.

explain: 재료나 색을 알맞게 섞어 어울리게 하는 일이에요. '색 배합', '재료 배합', '사료 배합'처럼 많이 써요. 그냥 섞는 '혼합'과 달리 비율이나 어울림을 생각한다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means mixing ingredients or colors in a suitable way so they go well together. It is commonly used in '색 배합', '재료 배합' and '사료 배합'. Unlike plain mixing, '혼합', it carries a sense of ratio and harmony.

examples.en: A caterpillar transforms into a butterfly.
The actor transformed into a villain in the movie.
On the weekend I will turn into a chef at home.
I bought a transforming robot toy.
I got a haircut and look completely different.
I was surprised that the plain bag turned into a party bag.

explain: '변하다'는 어떤 변화든 쓰지만 '변신하다'는 겉모습이나 역할이 확 달라질 때만 써요. 만화나 영화 이야기에 많이 나오고, 외모가 확 바뀐 친구에게 '완전 변신했네요!'라고 칭찬할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '변하다' covers any change, but '변신하다' is for a big shift in appearance or role. It is common in cartoons and movies, and you can praise a friend's new look with '완전 변신했네요!'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 한쪽 발꿈치를 축으로 빙그르르 돌아서셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher turned around smoothly, pivoting on one heel.
The child spun around and sat down, dizzy.

examples.ko: 무용수가 빙그르르 한 바퀴 돌고 인사했어요.
examples.en: The dancer twirled once and then took a bow.
The leaves spun round and round in the wind as they fell.
The top spun around and then stopped.

examples.ko: 눈앞이 빙그르르 도는 것 같아서 잠깐 앉았어요.
examples.en: Everything seemed to spin before my eyes, so I sat down for a moment.

explain: 둥글고 매끄럽게 한 바퀴 도는 모양을 나타내요. '빙글빙글'은 계속 도는 느낌이 강하고, '빙그르르'는 돌아서거나 한 바퀴 도는 동작에 잘 어울려요. 작은 느낌이면 '뱅그르르'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes turning around smoothly in a round motion. '빙글빙글' strongly suggests continuous spinning, while '빙그르르' suits a single turn or a swing around. The smaller, lighter version is '뱅그르르'.

examples.en: The pencil scratches softly on the paper.

examples.ko: 사과를 베어 물자 사각거리는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I bit into the apple, it made a crisp crunching sound.
The fallen leaves rustle under my feet, which feels nice.
In the library, I could only hear the sound of writing scratching.
The new blanket rustles softly and feels nice.
The ice crunched every time I chewed it.

explain: 연필로 쓸 때, 과일이나 얼음을 씹을 때처럼 얇고 단단한 것이 스치거나 부서지며 나는 가벼운 소리예요. 반복형 '사각사각'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the light sound of thin, firm things rubbing or breaking, such as writing with a pencil or chewing fruit or ice. The repeated form '사각사각' is also used often.

examples.en: The baby looked at its mom and smiled brightly.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 누구를 만나도 생글거리며 인사해요.
examples.en: That child greets everyone with a bright smile.
What's so good that you're smiling to yourself?
Seeing her smiling face made me feel better.
The clerk was smiling brightly, so I smiled along.

examples.ko: 동생은 칭찬을 듣고 하루 종일 생글거릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got praised and will probably be smiling all day.

explain: 소리 없이 눈과 입으로 부드럽고 밝게 웃는 모습이에요. '생글생글 웃다'라고도 하고, 아이나 젊은 사람의 환한 웃음에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes smiling softly and brightly with the eyes and mouth, without sound. People also say '생글생글 웃다', and it fits the cheerful smile of a child or young person.

examples.en: The company miniaturized the device and lowered the price too.
The research team shrank the sensor to the size of a fingernail.
To make the parts smaller, you need new materials.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 내년까지 장비를 소형화할 계획이에요.
examples.en: Our team plans to downsize the equipment by next year.

examples.ko: 어떻게 하면 배터리를 소형화할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: How can we make the battery smaller?

examples.ko: 자동차를 소형화하는 추세라서 작은 모델이 인기예요.
examples.en: There is a trend of downsizing cars, so small models are popular.

explain: '~을 소형화하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 저절로 작아질 때는 '작아지다'를 쓰고, 반대말은 '대형화하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it with an object, as in '~을 소형화하다'. When something just becomes small on its own, say '작아지다'. Its opposite is '대형화하다'.

examples.en: Big changes always come with risk.

examples.ko: 이 수술은 통증이 수반될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This surgery can come with pain.
I learned that responsibility comes with rights.

examples.ko: 비용이 수반되는 일은 미리 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell us ahead of time about anything that involves costs.
Growth is bound to come with difficulties.
A fever accompanied by a cough has lasted a week.

explain: 수반되다는 어떤 일에 다른 일이 자연스럽게 따라올 때 써요. '위험이 수반되다', '비용이 수반되다'처럼 주로 부정적이거나 중립적인 것이 따라올 때 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '따르다', '같이 오다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is used when one thing naturally brings another along with it. It is mostly used with negative or neutral things, such as 위험 or 비용. In speech, 따르다 or 같이 오다 is easier.

examples.ko: 아이가 손가락으로 반죽을 쿡쿡 눌러 봤어요.
examples.en: The child pressed the dough with a finger in deep pokes.
My younger sibling keeps poking my side.

examples.ko: 웃음을 참느라 쿡쿡 소리가 새어 나왔어요.
examples.en: I tried to hold back my laughter, but a snicker slipped out.

examples.ko: 감자가 익었는지 포크로 쿡쿡 찔러 보세요.
examples.en: Poke the potato with a fork to see if it's cooked.
My shoulder aches sharply, so I think I have to go to the hospital.
I'm digging the ground with a shovel in deep thrusts.

explain: 뾰족하거나 끝이 있는 것으로 깊이 찌르는 모습이에요. '콕콕'은 작고 가볍게 찍는 느낌이라 '쿡쿡'과 달라요. 웃음을 참으며 낮게 웃는 소리나, 몸이 욱신욱신 쑤시는 느낌에도 써요.
explain_en: It shows a pointed or tipped object being thrust in deeply. '콕콕' feels small and light, which is different from '쿡쿡'. It is also used for a stifled laugh and for the feeling of a throbbing ache.

examples.ko: 낡은 공장이 멋진 문화 공간으로 탈바꿈을 했어요.
examples.en: The old factory underwent a transformation into a cool cultural space.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 탈바꿈에 팬들이 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The fans were surprised by the singer's makeover.
This neighborhood needs a complete transformation.
A caterpillar becoming a butterfly is also a transformation.
The city's transformation was finished in five years.

examples.ko: 과감한 탈바꿈 덕분에 가게 손님이 두 배로 늘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the bold transformation, the shop's customers doubled.

explain: 모양이나 상태가 눈에 띄게 확 달라지는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '변화'보다 겉모습이나 성격이 크게 바뀐 느낌이 강해요. 애벌레가 나비가 되는 것처럼 곤충의 모습이 바뀌는 것에도 써요.
explain_en: It means the shape or state changes in a very noticeable way. It feels bigger than plain '변화' (change), as if the look or character was completely altered. It is also used for insects changing form, like a caterpillar turning into a butterfly.

en: with a puff or whoosh; in one sudden gust

examples.en: I blew out the candle with a puff.

examples.ko: 문을 열자 뜨거운 바람이 훅 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the door, a blast of hot air rushed in.
I blew on the hot soup again and again and ate it.

examples.ko: 추운 날 입김을 훅 내뱉으면 하얗게 보여요.
examples.en: On a cold day, if you breathe out in a puff, it shows up white.
I blew the dust away and it got in my eyes.

examples.ko: 식당에 들어서자 음식 냄새가 훅 풍겼어요.
examples.en: The smell of food hit me as I stepped into the restaurant.

explain: '훅 불다', '훅 끼치다'처럼 짧고 센 숨이나 열기, 냄새에 주로 써요. 여러 번 반복하면 '훅훅'이 돼요. 후후 부드럽게 부는 느낌과 달리 한 번에 세게 내뿜는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 훅 mostly goes with a short, strong breath, or with heat and smell, as in 훅 불다 and 훅 끼치다. Repeated, it becomes 훅훅. Unlike a soft 후후 blow, it feels like one strong burst.

examples.en: I flinched at a sudden voice calling from behind.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 제 질문에 흠칫하더니 대답을 피했어요.
examples.en: He flinched at my question and then avoided answering.

examples.ko: 차가운 물이 닿자 저도 모르게 흠칫하고 말았어요.
examples.en: When the cold water touched me, I flinched without meaning to.

examples.ko: 이름을 부르자 그는 흠칫하며 뒤를 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, he gave a start and turned around.

examples.ko: 어두운 길에서 그림자를 보고 흠칫한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once flinched at a shadow on a dark road.

examples.ko: 너무 놀라 흠칫하는 바람에 컵을 떨어뜨릴 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I was so startled that I flinched and almost dropped my cup.

explain: 놀라거나 찔려서 몸이 짧게 움찔하는 것이에요. '깜짝 놀라다'보다 작고 순간적인 반응이고, 속마음을 들켰을 때도 써요. '흠칫 멈추어 서다'처럼 부사 '흠칫'으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a short, involuntary jerk of the body from surprise or from being caught off guard. It is a smaller, more instant reaction than '깜짝 놀라다', and also fits when someone's secret is touched on. It often appears as the adverb '흠칫', as in '흠칫 멈추어 서다'.
